entry.title: Why Edge AI Research Needs Field Validation: Lessons from Replicating MIT CSAIL
entry.summary: I live in a reserved forest area in Tripura, Northeast India. Here, the "Cloud" is a luxury. With 4G hotspots with 1000ms+ latency, the AI tools the world takes for granted simply don't work. This forced me to look deeper into Efficient ML—not as a performance optimization, but as a survival necessity. The Replication Study: The "Forest" Data vs. The "Lab" Data: Connecting with MIT Faculty: I want to bridge the gap between "Efficient Algorithms" and "Infrastructural Resilience." I want to work to develop auto-ML techniques that are not just hardware-aware, but environment-aware—models that dynamically adjust precision based on available battery and real-time signal-to-noise ratios. I want to ensure that the AI revolution doesn't stop at the "Last Mile" of internet connectivity.

entry.title: The Real AI Divide Inside Companies is Clarity, Not Tools
entry.summary: As the Founder of ReThynk AI, I’ve noticed something uncomfortable. Inside companies, the AI divide is not: paid tools vs free tools technical vs non-technical prompt experts vs beginners The real divide is: people who can clearly define what they want vs people who can’t. AI rewards clarity. If I can define: the outcome the audience the constraints the standard of quality AI becomes predictable. If I can’t define those things, AI becomes random. That’s why some teams say: “AI is magic.” And others say: “AI is useless.” Same tool. Different clarity. So for businesses, democratisation of AI doesn’t start with buying tools. It starts with building a culture of clear thinking: clear goals clear owners clear definitions of done clear review standards When clarity becomes normal, AI becomes leverage for everyone: marketing, sales, HR, operations. That’s the real democratisation: making AI work for normal people inside normal teams.
